also.why: collapses definition and test into one object, so running the code is running the test.

beats.why: l40 says a type is defined by the propositions it satisfies, the same idea stated as a property rather than as the sharper, more infectious 'defining is testing'.

harms: a function with no cheap test becomes hard to admit
blurs the line between specification and verification, hiding which is trusted
statistical tests give false confidence of proof
candidates.instead_of: a definition that is only a body, with tests written separately and optionally later
candidates.quote: La idea central del tapp es que al declarar una funcion vos declaras que es lo que la funcion debe cumplir como un test y entonces es posible generar tests automaticos.
candidates.statement: Defining a function means stating, as runnable tests, what it must satisfy, so definition and verification are one act.

strongest.why: it recasts what it means to have a function: you do not have it until you have said, as runnable tests, what it must satisfy.

candidates.above_next: It is the single mechanism Luciano calls the core of Luthier, where C3's code-as-data is the older, broader frame it rides on.

also.why: economy: the type and the constructor stop being two confused things and become two uses of one.

beats.why: l382 structures a single law well, but it is a piece of the pattern, not the generative pattern itself.

harms: every value carries a certificate, costing memory and compute
the predicate may be undecidable or only testable, so 'checked' means different strengths
forces thinking in predicates even where a plain value would do
candidates.instead_of: types and their validating constructors declared as separate, hand-matched things
candidates.quote: lo primitivo es el predicado, y el tipo y el constructor se derivan de él mecánicamente. No son dos cosas que se confunden bajo un nombre; son dos usos de una sola cosa.
candidates.statement: Make the predicate the primitive, and derive the certified type, its sole constructor and its forgetful projection from it.

strongest.why: one primitive, a predicate over a material, generates type, constructor and forget mechanically, unifying values, functions and whole programs.

candidates.above_next: It is a larger ontological commitment than the specific forgetting machinery that follows, which lives inside it.

also.why: the syntax is a data like any inductive type, so the core explains itself, metacircular.

beats.why: l228 says many operations apply to code, which is a consequence of code-as-data rather than the frame-opening idea itself.

harms: homoiconicity invites self-modification and self-hacking
a core that is its own data is harder to keep consistent
power tempts cleverness over clarity
candidates.instead_of: code as an opaque artifact the language runs but cannot hold or operate on
candidates.quote: La idea de que el codigo sea dato es muy, pero muy fuerte en cuanto a la flexibilidad que ofrece pero es notable que los lenguajes modernos no sigan ese camino Lispeano.
candidates.statement: Hold a program's code as a value of an ordinary data type, so code and data are the same kind of thing.

strongest.why: erasing the code/data line lets a program hold, inspect and transform its own code as an ordinary value, reorganizing what a program is.

candidates.above_next: It structures the whole type machinery, where C5's equivalence is the thing forgetting must commute with, downstream of it.

also.why: it unifies mean, projection, execution and compilation as instances of one operation, forgetting.

beats.why: l196 observes that different forgetting functions optimize different things, a corollary of the stronger claim that the choice of forgetting is the language.

harms: choosing the wrong forgetful functor silently changes the language's meaning
forgetting is non-invertible, so information is lost for good
an ill-defined forgetting degenerates into crude truncation Luciano rejects
candidates.instead_of: forgetting as an ad hoc cleanup, with the language fixed independently of it
candidates.quote: de qué función de olvido le aplicás a los tipos, es un, digamos, eso te define básicamente el lenguaje que estás hablando ... los functores de olvido serían, digamos, uno de los componentes más importantes de Luthier
candidates.statement: Treat the choice of what to forget from a type as the thing that defines the language you are speaking.

strongest.why: it reframes a language as defined by what it chooses to forget, turning the forgetful functor from a side tool into the identity of the language.

candidates.above_next: It is a sharp reframe of execution, where C6 reframes the purpose of the whole language and reaches wider.

also.why: it dissolves the execution/proof divide into one act, elegant and spare.

beats.why: l218 enumerates levels of equivalence, useful but a taxonomy inside the deeper claim that execution itself is equivalence-checking.

harms: demoting execution may make the language impractical for real computation
verifying equivalence is undecidable in general
users wanting to just run things face a conceptual detour
candidates.instead_of: execution as a separate operational act distinct from reasoning about equivalence
candidates.quote: Hay una idea, que la matemática no ejecuta, porque lo único que hace es verificar equivalencias. Entonces, bueno, sí, la ejecución en Luthier sería esa verificación de equivalencias
candidates.statement: Make execution the verification of equivalences, following mathematics, which does not run but only verifies.

strongest.why: it redefines running a program as verifying equivalences, importing mathematics' stance that nothing executes, equivalences are only checked.

candidates.above_next: It states the language's purpose, broader than the declarative-plus-optimizer mechanism that serves it.

also.why: it makes the unit of expression a discipline's invariant rather than an algorithm or value.

beats.why: l238, a language where ideas are first-class, is close but more diffuse than the specific aim of expressing invariances.

harms: 'invariance of a discipline' is vague and hard to pin down operationally
risks the project growing to cover the whole universe and becoming useless
privileges domains with clean invariances over messy ones
candidates.instead_of: a language that expresses computations or statistical patterns, not the invariants behind them
candidates.quote: la idea de luthier es expresar invarianzas de los de las disciplinas
candidates.statement: Aim the language at expressing the invariances of each discipline, as a relator of invariances.

strongest.why: it names what moves the author: a language that relates the invariances of each field, set against statistical predictors that only guess.

candidates.above_next: It opens a whole operational frame, where C8 is one elegant primitive within such a design.

also.why: it makes the trade-off between clarity and speed explicit and the machine's, not hidden in the programmer's head.

beats.why: l134, the performance database, is the implementation substrate for this idea rather than the reframe itself.

harms: maintaining many paths and their cost estimates is heavy machinery
a priori cost estimation is the hardest open problem, maybe unsolvable well
the run database can grow monstrous and paralyzing
candidates.instead_of: writing one implementation and committing to its performance by hand
candidates.quote: que Luthier sea, en el fondo, una forma de ser a la vez un lenguaje declarativo y una herramienta de optimización. O sea, que vos declares lo que querés hacer, que sigan más decir las fórmulas, y después internamente baraja distintas formas de implementar eso, pero eso lo hace abiertamente
candidates.statement: Let the programmer declare what they want and have the engine openly weigh many equivalent implementation paths by estimated cost.

strongest.why: it splits a program into what it means (declared) and how it runs (openly chosen among estimated paths), reorganizing the frame of writing code.

candidates.above_next: It is a crisp unification, where C9 is the more foundational logical stance the whole type system rests on.

also.why: its semantics is exactly 'do not execute until defined', so dead and pending code sit harmlessly.

beats.why: l226 states the 'no execution until defined' rule, which the hole subsumes and sharpens into a single primitive.

harms: overloading one construct with five meanings can confuse readers
no way to mark intention means external vs unwritten is indistinguishable
a program full of holes may typecheck yet do nothing
candidates.instead_of: separate language features for axioms, inputs, foreign calls, stubs and unused code
candidates.quote: el **hueco**: una definición con tipo y sin cuerpo, `f : A → B := ?`. Una sola cosa cumple cinco papeles: axioma, input del programa, función externa que el entorno llena, definición pendiente, código muerto. Tu principio "no ejecutás hasta que está definido" es su semántica exacta
candidates.statement: Let a bodyless typed declaration be the one construct that serves as axiom, input, external function, pending definition and dead code at once.

strongest.why: one construct, a bodyless declaration, collapses five roles that other languages keep as separate features.

candidates.above_next: It is the logical foundation, where C10 is the stylistic and architectural discipline laid on top.

also.why: it takes a stance that a program should carry the guarantee of what it claims, not just do it.

beats.why: l45, laws stated universally on a type, is an application of the propositions-as-types view rather than the view itself.

harms: Curry-Howard raises the entry cost for ordinary programmers
making code its own proof demands discipline most code cannot pay
proof obligations can balloon with each dependent composition
candidates.instead_of: types as mere data shapes, with correctness argued outside the code
candidates.quote: los tipos tienen que ser conceptos, tipos como proposiciones y los tipos incluyen también funciones, funciones y funciones de orden superior
candidates.statement: Make types propositions and terms their proofs, so the code is its own mathematical demonstration.

strongest.why: types as propositions and code as its own proof fuses programming and proving, validating logic before a line runs.

also.why: a language executable with pencil and paper insists the programmer can always understand what runs.

beats.why: l154, keeping only types and functions, is one concrete reduction inside the broader principle of few founding components.

harms: extreme minimalism can push complexity onto unreadable library layers
'executable by hand' may forbid features users want
few primitives risks cryptic error messages
candidates.instead_of: a rich primitive set with special-cased features and sugar in the core
candidates.quote: El minimalismo está en los componentes fundantes y después a partir de esos componentes fundantes vos construís un edificio enorme.
candidates.statement: Keep the founding components few and hand-executable, and build the whole edifice of complex concepts from them.

strongest.why: minimalism in the founding components, from which a huge edifice is built, is the classic beauty of economy.
